root_cause.text: pressure_write() accesses the cgroup_file_ctx pointer (of->priv) without holding cgroup_mutex, allowing a concurrent cgroup_file_release() to free the memory and set of->priv to NULL, leading to use-after-free or NULL dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description details the race: CPU0 reads ctx = of->priv in pressure_write() before acquiring cgroup_mutex, while CPU1 in cgroup_file_release() frees ctx and sets of->priv = NULL under cgroup_mutex. The second scenario shows ctx can become NULL after a blocking point, causing NULL dereference. The patch moves ctx retrieval after cgroup_kn_lock_live() (which acquires cgroup_mutex) and adds a NULL check for safety.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reference counting and locking in pressure_write by removing redundant cgroup_get/put and adding a NULL check for ctx.
intent_record.what: Moved ctx declaration after locking; added ret variable and null check for ctx; replaced early returns with goto out_unlock; removed cgroup_get and cgroup_put calls; deferred lock release to out_unlock.
intent_record.how: The function now holds the cgroup lock throughout execution instead of releasing it early, and no longer takes an extra reference on the cgroup. Error paths set ret and jump to out_unlock, which releases the lock. A null check on ctx prevents dereference. Previously taken references are eliminated, changing resource management.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `cgroup_pressure_write()`, after `cgroup_kn_unlock(of->kn)` releases `cgroup_mutex`, the function calls `psi_trigger_replace(&of->priv, new)` without holding any lock. This allows a concurrent `cgroup_pressure_release()` (via `psi_trigger_replace(&of->priv, NULL)`) to free `of->priv`, leading to a use-after-free or NULL dereference. Similarly, `cgroup_pressure_poll()` accesses `of->priv` in `psi_trigger_poll()` without any lock. The fix is not present in this commit.
